\cataloguefield{section}{Capability Overview}

Operational coordination connects available resources with actual care-setting constraints and observable work progression. Bed state, local capacity, aggregate capacity, transport and discharge remain separate abilities even when they exchange the same milestones.


\cataloguefield{section}{Definition — Proposed}

Represent and coordinate care-setting flow, operational resources, workforce participation, movement and service-delivery preparedness.


\cataloguefield{section}{Intent}

Make operational constraints and progression visible enough to coordinate the care-delivery responsibilities actually assigned to Harmonia.


\cataloguefield{section}{Boundary}

Coordination owns only explicitly assigned operational activity. It does not originate clinical clearance, determine clinical work or take workforce and resource governance from their sources.

It makes delays, waiting and completion context visible alongside service-specific capacity responsibilities. This is real-world clinic operation, distinct from the technical queueing machinery that might realise the information flow.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Operational queue progression does not determine clinical priority or own the clinician's worklist.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Process Overview}

This Process follows an individual's operational passage through the clinic. Waiting, rooming, consultation and departure have different implications for flow and communication, while the clinic's overall session has its own state. The progression is therefore patient-specific operational context rather than a complete account of clinic capacity or clinical priority.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Clinic \& Practice Operations}}



\item
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the movement and state tracking of outpatients through an ambulatory specialty clinic session.



\item
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Scheduled → Patient Arrived → Checked-In → Roomed /\allowbreak{} Pre-Consult → Consultation In-Progress → Consultation Concluded → Departed



\item
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Scheduled}}: Appointment booked on session list.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Patient Arrived}}: Patient enters waiting area.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Checked-In}}: Reception verifies demographics and marks patient ready.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Roomed / Pre-Consult}}: Nursing staff record baseline vitals and room patient.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Consultation In-Progress}}: Clinician actively conducting consultation.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Consultation Concluded}}: Clinical discussion finished; follow-up orders placed.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Departed}}: Patient checks out and departs clinic facility.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Ward Operations coordinates ward occupancy and care-place context and assembles the information needed around shift changes. Its responsibility includes the ward-specific meaning of capacity and patient flow rather than a generic resource counter. It can make pending concerns and tasks visible without becoming the authority managing clinical handover.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Handover information assembly is distinct from performing or managing handover. Context-specific capacity remains with Ward Operations.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Correlated ward state and contextual information materially support operational continuity.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns coordinate the local flow, session state and capacity semantics of a care-delivery setting. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Theatre Operations integrates surgical case progression and the operational consequences relevant to portering, sterilisation and recovery participants. It gives reported milestones an operational coordination context without originating the surgical acts they describe. Theatre-specific capacity remains a business responsibility even when shared information machinery supports several service contexts.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Tracking incision or recovery information does not authorise surgery or transfer control of the clinical procedure.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Milestone-driven operational notifications materially connect supporting activity around the theatre service.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns coordinate the local flow, session state and capacity semantics of a care-delivery setting. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Process Overview}

Theatre case progression follows reported milestones of the surgical encounter so that supporting participants can coordinate around the actual situation. The state account concerns what the clinical service reports has occurred. It does not make the integration mechanism the actor administering anaesthesia, performing surgery or managing clinical handover.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Theatre Operations}}



\item
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the perioperative operational milestones of a surgical procedure within the operating theatre suite.



\item
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Case Called → In Anaesthetic Bay → Anaesthesia Commenced → Patient in Theatre → Knife-to-Skin → Procedure Finished → In PACU Recovery → Ward Handover Complete



\item
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Case Called}}: Theatre team requests ward to send patient for surgery.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{In Anaesthetic Bay}}: Patient arrives in theatre holding and identity/\allowbreak{}consent verified.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Anaesthesia Commenced}}: Anaesthetic induction underway.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Patient in Theatre}}: Patient transferred onto operating table.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Knife-to-Skin}}: Surgical incision initiated (operative start).



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Procedure Finished}}: Wound closure completed and dressings applied.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{In PACU Recovery}}: Patient monitored in post-anaesthesia care unit.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Ward Handover Complete}}: Post-operative clinical handover to inpatient ward completed.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

This capability maintains the operational context of emergency places, waits and length-of-stay milestones. It supports understanding of occupancy and impediments in the department while keeping capacity's emergency-service meaning intact. Its concern differs from Emergency Care's clinical presentation context, even though both can refer to the same patient encounter.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Operational timing and escalation do not determine triage or acquire clinical decision authority.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Care-place state and operational waiting information materially support coordination of the emergency service.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns coordinate the local flow, session state and capacity semantics of a care-delivery setting. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Outpatient Operations integrates arrival events and follow-up requirements generated as clinics progress. It connects a person's operational presence with the relevant service context and makes post-clinic booking or diagnostic needs available for subsequent activity. The responsibility retains outpatient-specific capacity semantics without requiring a separate arrival Function where approved reusable composition suffices.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

An arrival does not establish consultation completion, and a captured follow-up requirement does not perform the clinical activity.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Arrival and clinic-outcome information materially connect outpatient progression to care coordination.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns coordinate the local flow, session state and capacity semantics of a care-delivery setting. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\emph{Capacity boundary}: Operational coordination does not acquire authoritative booking/\allowbreak{}rostering or clinical-work management. Room-occupancy query remains narrower than the capacity responsibility; no enlarged exposure or new named Service is inferred.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Bed \& Care-Place Management maintains operational place state and the turnover progression that makes a place usable again. Vacancy, reservation, cleaning and readiness must remain distinguishable so that an empty bed is not automatically treated as available for allocation. Notifications expose meaningful readiness changes to the responsible operational participants.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Intent}

Support credible care-place decisions using governed state rather than physical presence alone.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

A ready bed does not establish service-level capacity or collective readiness, and place state does not determine clinical suitability or care responsibility.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Governed place-state progression and operational notification are substantive assigned platform responsibilities.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns relate operational care-place and equipment state to the coordinated view of service demand and capacity. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Process Overview}

Bed turnover connects the release of a care place with the operational work needed to return it to use. Its progression preserves the difference between vacancy, cleaning and readiness. A place can be empty while work remains outstanding, and a completed turnover does not by itself prove that the service has capacity for the next patient.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Bed \& Care-Place Management}}



\item
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the rapid physical turnover, cleaning, sanitisation, and re-allocation of inpatient and emergency care-places.



\item
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Bed Vacated → Cleaning Dispatched → Sanitisation In-Progress → Terminal Cleaning Verified → Bed Ready /\allowbreak{} Available → Bed Allocated /\allowbreak{} Occupied



\item
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Bed Vacated}}: Prior patient discharged or transferred.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Cleaning Dispatched}}: Cleaning job allocated to environmental services team.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Sanitisation In-Progress}}: Ward cleaning or isolation decontamination underway.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Terminal Cleaning Verified}}: Ward coordinator or supervisor verifies care-place readiness.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Bed Ready / Available}}: Bed marked available for incoming patient allocation.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Bed Allocated / Occupied}}: Incoming patient allocated and physically placed in bed.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Clinical Resource Management integrates location and allocation information for shared clinical equipment. It makes the current operational resource context available rather than treating device inventory as proof that equipment can be used for a particular need. The responsibility supports coordination while retaining the distinction between resource state and a service's capacity.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Equipment tracking does not acquire enterprise asset ownership, maintenance responsibility or clinical authority to use it.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Dynamic equipment context materially supports operational coordination across care environments.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns relate operational care-place and equipment state to the coordinated view of service demand and capacity. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Service Capacity Management provides a higher-order view by aggregating capacity information across services and facilities. It can consider occupancy, waits and diversion while preserving the service-specific meaning of the underlying capacity. Its purpose is not to erase differences between clinic, ward, theatre, emergency, outpatient and mobile-service operation.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Consuming contextual capacity does not acquire the originating capacity-management responsibility or infer capacity solely from resource counts.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Cross-service operational visibility materially supports coordination while source service contexts retain their authority.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns relate operational care-place and equipment state to the coordinated view of service demand and capacity. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Collective readiness depends on suitable workforce, spaces, equipment, materials and supporting services. This proposal evaluates their joint availability for an offering without treating one available bed, an operating-hours declaration or aggregate capacity as service readiness.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition — Proposed}

Assemble the dependency evidence needed to determine and communicate whether a defined service offering is operationally ready in a particular context.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Intent}

Distinguish collective service deliverability from nominal availability or readiness of any single dependency.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Contributing capabilities retain source readiness and resource management. Clinical go/\allowbreak{}no-go decisions and service governance are not granted by this information-based coordination.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Review Confidence}
Low; applies to the proposal, not to preserved canonical meaning.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Derivation Provenance}
Inferred from bounded responsibilities and their semantic decomposition. AI architectural synthesis under the explicitly authorised Step 2 task \hyperref[evidence:a4c0900c47c945d9]{business-capabilities.md:403}; \hyperref[evidence:be61392fefb4bb10]{information-responsibility.md:34}

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Boundary}

Readiness evidence does not originate clinical clearance or transfer resource management.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Clinical Workforce Management is retained as an Adjacent operational context for the workforce on which services depend. The current enabling catalogue does not assign an atomic Feature set. Its presence allows workforce constraints to be recognised without treating integration of workforce facts as authority to govern employment, coverage or clinical allocation.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

No new workforce system responsibility or complete CT ancestry is inferred from this contextual entry.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Adjacent standing reflects contextual participation rather than management of the workforce itself.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns make workforce availability, coverage and eligible operational work participation usable in coordination. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Mobile Staff Management integrates with external business mobile-work mechanisms and receives visit progression and safety milestones. Its established dispatch Feature exchanges assignment, dispatch and status information with the relevant worker context. This is an information integration boundary around mobile activity, rather than a platform claim to decide the clinician's work.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Harmonia does not determine clinical allocation, handover or EMR worklists. External work/\allowbreak{}task language does not redefine the internal Synthetic Task.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Mobile assignment and progression exchanges materially connect roving activity to the wider care environment within that bounded integration role.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns make workforce availability, coverage and eligible operational work participation usable in coordination. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

On-Call Management resolves the active provider for a specialty, service or hospital at the relevant time. It turns changing coverage information into usable routing context so that operational communication can reach the intended capacity. This differs from authoring the roster or deciding who is professionally qualified for the requested activity.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Being on call does not by itself establish clinical privilege or assignment of a particular care responsibility.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Current provider resolution materially enables appropriate contact and routing across operational boundaries.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns make workforce availability, coverage and eligible operational work participation usable in coordination. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Feature Overview}

Active on-call resolution identifies the current provider in the required specialty and hospital context. It supports correct routing at the relevant time without authoring the roster or treating current coverage as proof of qualification, privilege or responsibility acceptance.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

Resolve currently active on-call specialists, registrars, and operational managers for a given specialty and hospital at any point in time.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Work Allocation \& Dispatch progresses authorised operational work from a recognised requirement through matching, dispatch, acknowledgement and oversight. It distinguishes an instantiated work item from its assignment and from evidence of performance, allowing stalled activity to be identified and escalated. Examples such as cleaning or transport concern real-world support work, not technical message queues.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Intent}

Make operational work progression accountable from requirement to reported outcome within applicable policy and role constraints.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

This assignment responsibility does not confer clinical work allocation, qualification or privilege. A technical receipt has only its interaction contract's meaning.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Governed operational work progression is a substantive platform responsibility supporting the Core classification.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns make workforce availability, coverage and eligible operational work participation usable in coordination. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Feature Overview}

Work-item instantiation gives an authorised operational requirement an identifiable unit of work. It distinguishes recognising that support activity is needed from assigning it, dispatching it and recording its completion; a clinical trigger does not make the resulting support item clinical work authority.

Instantiate operational units of work from clinical triggers (e.g., bed cleaning required, specimen transport required).

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Process Overview}

Operational work progression makes the path from a recognised support requirement to assigned and reported work explicit. Acknowledgement and activity progress help distinguish a dispatch from actual performance and expose impediments requiring operational attention. This responsibility remains bounded to authorised support work rather than ownership of the clinician's worklist.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Work Allocation \& Dispatch}}



\item
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the dispatch, assignment, execution, and completion of facility operational jobs (e.g., equipment moves, waste removal, linen supply).



\item
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Work Requested → Queued in Dispatch → Assigned to Worker → Job Accepted → Work In-Progress → Work Completed /\allowbreak{} Aborted



\item
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Work Requested}}: Facility support task submitted by clinical unit.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Queued in Dispatch}}: Job prioritized in operational queue.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Assigned to Worker}}: Job allocated to specific staff member or team.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Job Accepted}}: Worker acknowledges dispatch on mobile device.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Work In-Progress}}: Task actively being executed.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Work Completed / Aborted}}: Job marked finished or formally cancelled with reason.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

Clinical Supervision is a Reference context for the professional supervision of care activity. Its inclusion locates that enterprise responsibility without assigning a Harmonia supervision Feature or clinical-work mandate. Operational visibility into activity and qualifications can be useful context without becoming the professional act of supervising practice.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Workflow oversight or platform escalation does not confer clinical supervision or responsibility for clinical adequacy.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns represent learning, competence, professional-standing checks and separately governed operational access qualifications. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

Medium; applies to the proposal, not to preserved canonical meaning.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Process Overview}

Patient transport progression records the physical journey from a movement request through departure, transit and destination arrival. Its checkpoints allow operational participants to follow the journey with relevant mobility context intact. Arrival closes a movement concern only under its applicable scope; it does not establish clinical handover or destination acceptance of care responsibility.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Patient Transport}}



\item
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the physical portering and transport of patients between hospital departments, wards, diagnostic suites, and external facilities.



\item
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Transport Requested → Porter Dispatched → Patient Collected → In-Transit → Delivered at Destination → Clinical Handover Complete



\item
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Transport Requested}}: Clinical unit books wheelchair, bed, or ambulance transport.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Porter Dispatched}}: Wardsperson assigned and en route to pickup location.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Patient Collected}}: Patient identity verified and transfer initiated.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Transit}}: Patient actively moving through facility corridors or ambulance transit.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Delivered at Destination}}: Patient arrives at target diagnostic suite or ward.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Handover Complete}}: Safe custody and clinical briefing transferred to receiving staff.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Clinical Logistics Coordination integrates the movement and custody context of clinical material, notably specimen pickup, transport conditions and laboratory delivery. It keeps a material's journey connected to the fulfilment context requiring it. This enables clinical logistics to be followed without reducing specimen integrity to a delivery timestamp alone.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Tracking material movement does not perform diagnostic interpretation or establish general enterprise supply-chain ownership.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Custody and transport information materially support diagnostic continuity and appropriate interpretation of specimen handling.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns coordinate movement of people/\allowbreak{}materials and operational departure readiness across care boundaries. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Process Overview}

Specimen transport preserves the movement and custody account connecting collection context with laboratory receipt. It makes the journey of the material explainable rather than reducing it to a sent/\allowbreak{}received pair. Delivery remains distinct from specimen acceptance, diagnostic performance and the eventual professional interpretation of its evidence.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Logistics Coordination}}



\item
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the physical courier chain-of-custody, transport, and delivery of pathology bio-specimens, blood products, and surgical biopsies.



\item
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Specimen Packaged → Courier Dispatched → Chain-of-Custody Signed → In-Transit (Monitored) → Lab Ingress Received → Specimen Accepted



\item
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Specimen Packaged}}: Clinical unit packages bio-sample with barcode manifest.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Courier Dispatched}}: Courier route assigned for pickup.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Chain-of-Custody Signed}}: Courier scans barcode and accepts legal custody.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Transit (Monitored)}}: Specimen in transit under temperature/\allowbreak{}time constraints.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Lab Ingress Received}}: Central pathology specimen reception logs physical receipt.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Specimen Accepted}}: Specimen integrity verified and passed to analytical track.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Discharge Management coordinates the reported milestones needed around discharge, including medication supply, transport and home-care confirmations. It makes readiness and impediments visible across disciplines and communicates departure information when physical exit occurs. The responsibility preserves a distinction between gathering confirmations and making the clinical decision that discharge is appropriate.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Milestone completion does not transfer clinical responsibility or prove the receiving provider accepted it. Readiness, exit and clinical decision authority remain distinct.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Cross-team milestone coordination and departure notification are substantive assigned platform responsibilities.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns coordinate movement of people/\allowbreak{}materials and operational departure readiness across care boundaries. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Process Overview}

Discharge progression coordinates the confirmations and practical requirements around leaving care. Clinical readiness, medications, destination arrangements and transport are related but distinct contributions, and the source progression retains its stated local applicability. Operational coordination does not originate the clinical discharge decision or prove that another provider assumed responsibility.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Discharge Management}}



\item
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the multidisciplinary coordination of patient discharge planning, pharmacy reconciliation, transport, and community handover.



\item
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Discharge Planning Initiated → Clinical Readiness Confirmed → Medications Reconciled → Transport \& Services Booked → Discharge Summary Signed → Physically Departed   (Illustrative preparation; publication, authorisation and exit distinct)



\item
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharge Planning Initiated}}: Estimated Date of Discharge (EDD) set on admission.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Readiness Confirmed}}: Attending medical team declares patient fit for discharge.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Medications Reconciled}}: Hospital pharmacy reconciles and dispenses discharge medications.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Transport \& Services Booked}}: Community nursing, home equipment, and patient transport booked.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharge Summary Signed}}: Applicable signed summary is available/\allowbreak{}published and may be communicated before departure where the Business behaviour requires it; signing, finalisation, publication and discharge authorisation remain distinct.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Physically Departed}}: Confirmed physical exit triggers departure notifications, updated bed-state communication and finalised-summary dispatch to external care providers under \texttt{\seqsplit{FEAT-HSO-29}}; care-place turnover follows its own responsibility.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Timing reconciliation}: Preparation, information availability/\allowbreak{}publication, applicable discharge authorisation and physical exit are distinct. Earlier preparation/\allowbreak{}communication is permitted; it does not realise a Feature triggered by confirmed exit. This illustrated local pathway establishes neither universal publication timing nor a universal discharge state machine, and adds no inferred publication event or authorisation state.



\item
\textbf{Preserved uncertainty}: Summary signing and finalisation are not universal equivalents. Detailed applicability, discharge-authority workflows and timing beyond the established preparation/\allowbreak{}confirmed-exit distinction remain unestablished.



\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

This frame makes a managed record usable over time and across authorised purposes. It separates clinical synthesis, binary-content association, external exchange, semantic definitions, privacy and evidence so that none becomes an undifferentiated information utility.


\cataloguefield{section}{Definition — Proposed}

Preserve, find, exchange, qualify and protect health information and the governed definitions needed to interpret it.


\cataloguefield{section}{Intent}

Keep managed health information usable and attributable across time, boundaries and authorised purposes.


\cataloguefield{section}{Boundary}

Preservation, custody, discoverability and presentation do not confer originating fact authority. Clinical documentation administration and clinical-context use retain their own responsibilities.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Patient Clinical Record provides a governed longitudinal representation across encounters, providers and source systems. Assembly supplies the timeline, active access supports current care context, and durable preservation retains the history of what Harmonia received, knew or managed. These contributions are complementary: a responsive working view must not become the authority for durable history.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Intent}

Make cross-institutional information usable over time without erasing source provenance or prior knowledge through correction.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Preservation does not originate clinical facts. Active distributed access and authoritative durable preservation remain separate under AX-05.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Longitudinal assembly, active access and governed durable history are direct information-management responsibilities within the Core boundary.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns maintain governed longitudinal synthesis and the associations needed to use its constituent clinical information safely. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition — Proposed}

Associate, resolve, retrieve and assemble binary content needed to use managed clinical or operational information.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Intent}

Obtain the content needed to use a managed information item without assuming where every payload is physically held.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

As a BEC, Health Information Exchange provides reusable information-movement enablement through submission, retrieval mediation, addressed distribution and syndication. The models distinguish sending to a participant, requesting information, deliberately distributing to named recipients and publishing changes to matching subscribers. Their common responsibility is the exchange context, including routing and delivery state, rather than the business meaning of every payload.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

The capability owns exchange transaction state without acquiring clinical-document ownership. Its name collision with the BC remains unresolved; exchange egress ends management of the emitted representation.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Multi-party exchange and per-destination delivery tracking are substantive Core responsibilities, bounded by the external contract and originating information authority.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns make governed health information discoverable and exchangeable under explicit internal and external contracts. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Naming Decision}

Distinguishes reusable Harmonia exchange enablement from the organisational BC of the same governed name; identity and responsibility remain Canonical.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Health Information Access enables authorised discovery and retrieval across clinical information. It combines semantic search and discrete retrieval with access-qualified filtering so that a discoverable item is not automatically disclosable. It consumes established policy and consent determinations rather than making the search interface an alternative security authority.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Retrieval alone does not realise the filtering Feature. Unestablished Feature associations remain unestablished even where the behaviour shares the same owner.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance — v0.1 explanation}

Responsive governed access is a direct platform responsibility. The approved support to Individual Care Delivery remains bounded and does not establish runtime dependencies for every clinical ability.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns make governed health information discoverable and exchangeable under explicit internal and external contracts. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Health Information Communication supplies standards-based transmission mediation between participating parties. It addresses protocol-facing transaction coordination and technical error handling while the business interaction retains its own meaning and authority. This differentiates the communication mechanism from the exchange model and from the clinical or operational purpose of the message.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Transport mediation does not own every communicated interaction or payload. External contracts must preserve standards semantics and exclude private operational metadata.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Standards-conformant communication boundaries are a direct interoperability responsibility.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns make governed health information discoverable and exchangeable under explicit internal and external contracts. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Clinical Knowledge Services resolves governed clinical concepts and applies governed terminology mappings. It makes codes usable across local and standard semantic systems while retaining their source meaning. The responsibility is semantic reference and mapping enablement, distinct from formulating reusable clinical knowledge or applying that knowledge to an individual.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Code translation does not establish equivalence beyond the governed map or confer clinical decision authority.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Concept resolution and mapping materially support meaningful information exchange and interpretation across regional systems.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns govern the definitions, terminology and reference content that make healthcare information consistently interpretable. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Information Design Governance maintains canonical definitions, semantic bindings, exchange profiles and the conformance rules applied to representations. It makes meaning and constraints available across regional information flows so that an accepted technical format is not mistaken for semantic correctness. Governance and verification remain distinguishable from the clinical facts represented.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Consumers of definitions do not acquire their semantic authority, and conformance checking does not establish clinical truth or permission to disclose.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Governed semantics and representation conformance are direct platform responsibilities that constrain both internal use and boundary exchange.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns govern the definitions, terminology and reference content that make healthcare information consistently interpretable. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Health Information Control establishes the policy and security basis for governed information operations. Default-deny authority evaluation, consent constraints, security-context propagation and security-significant evidence have distinct purposes: deciding permission, retaining restrictions, carrying attributable operational context and preserving required evidence. The capability makes security intrinsic to the operation rather than optional presentation behaviour.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Security context is operational context and does not automatically become resource content. Security-context validation has no invented one-to-one mapping to propagation, and audit recording is not an assurance conclusion.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Assigned policy enforcement and attributable context are substantive Core responsibilities across managed operations.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns apply information-use policy and preserve the accountability context needed for governed health-information activity. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

It provides continuity of context rather than independently deciding permission for every downstream action. The nearby validation Service has its own declared exposure; juxtaposition does not establish an exact one-to-one implementation relationship.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Mandatory evidence capture has its own policy-governed platform authority and must remain possible when the audited identity is denied an action. The captured fact is distinguished from debug output and the identity whose activity is recorded.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition — Proposed}

Capture required security- and information-significant activity as governed, attributable audit evidence.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Intent}

Ensure required significant activity evidence can be captured under the authority specifically assigned to that responsibility.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

The specific intrinsic authority for mandatory audit capture is not generalised to other activities. Capture is not an assurance finding and cannot expose unmasked PHI in diagnostic logs.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition — Proposed}

Prepare, convey and track required population-health notifications from applicable governed source information.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Intent}

Keep the applicable notification duty and the observed communication disposition traceable to each other.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Does not determine population-health findings, create statutory obligations or equate transport delivery with discharge of notification duty.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Review Confidence}
Medium; applies to the proposal, not to preserved canonical meaning.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Planners need comparable time- and service-qualified observations from multiple operating settings. This ability prepares those projections while leaving the interpretation of required future capacity and distribution with the planning authority.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition — Proposed}

Supply qualified demand, utilisation and capacity evidence to responsible health-service planning activities.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Intent}

Give planners qualified observed evidence without predetermining the planning judgement.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Observed utilisation, operational capacity and planned capacity are distinct; information provision does not commission services or allocate resources.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Review Confidence}

People discuss information, inspect it, make authorised decisions and undertake work. Those interactions need reusable coordination and temporal context, while entity-relative progression and activity design retain distinct semantics from message exchange and screen rendering.


\cataloguefield{section}{Definition — Proposed}

Enable contextual human interaction, collaboration and the definition and progression of governed operational activity.


\cataloguefield{section}{Intent}

Allow people and automated participants to interact and progress authorised work with intelligible context and accountability.


\cataloguefield{section}{Boundary}

Conversation is not a clinical record, presentation is not authority, and generic work coordination does not determine clinical work or own its outcome.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Clinical Collaboration provides secure multidisciplinary spaces bound to clinical context, including governed access to longitudinal information during discussion. Its purpose is contextual conversation between care participants rather than a separate source of authoritative clinical facts. A statement in a conversation remains discourse until explicitly authored through the governed record boundary.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Channel metadata must remain free of PHI. The source Function's mention of managing clinical handovers conflicts with the metamodel's clinical-work boundary; both are preserved for review without assigning that authority here.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

LHR-aware collaboration and controlled contextual queries are substantive Core responsibilities, distinct from clinical practice or record authorship.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns support contextual discussion and human interaction with governed information and activity. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

Metadata governance keeps patient names, identifiers and sensitive detail out of collaboration titles, topics and aliases. Opaque references preserve useful contextual association without placing PHI in broadly visible channel metadata or diagnostic surfaces.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

Ensure collaboration channel titles, topics, and aliases use opaque identifiers free of patient names, MRNs, or sensitive details.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Feature Overview}

A message may convey existing information or an explicit interaction may derive a new managed consequence. The distinction preserves collaboration-native records while routing governed consequences to their accountable responsibility.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition — Proposed}

Qualify when a defined collaboration interaction creates a new governed information or activity consequence.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Boundary}

Conversation presence, display or read receipt does not itself make a clinical decision, approval or final record.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

This behaviour changes or exposes the bounded concern of Clinical Collaboration, rather than inheriting an adjacent responsibility.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Derivation Provenance}
Inferred from capability-specific behaviour, v0.3 inspection and current architectural evidence. AI architectural synthesis under the explicitly authorised Step 2 task \hyperref[evidence:1fd96e59a1290815]{agora-omilia-collaboration.md:25}; \hyperref[evidence:be61392fefb4bb10]{information-responsibility.md:10}

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

General Collaboration provides secure operational messaging for departmental, administrative and facility-support participants. It gives non-clinical coordination an interaction context without assuming every discussion requires a patient-linked clinical workspace. Its role is communication enablement rather than ownership of the support activity being discussed.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Conversation does not assign operational authority, complete work or become an authoritative record merely through retention.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Operational messaging materially enables coordination while the participants' business responsibilities remain external to the collaboration mechanism.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns support contextual discussion and human interaction with governed information and activity. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Presentation Services supplies contextual human interaction through clinical timelines, directory views and operational dashboards. It makes governed information usable by people while consuming the identity, security and clinical context established elsewhere. The responsibility is the interaction and presentation experience rather than a new authority for the information shown.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Presentation does not own authentication, credential storage, consent decisions, EMPI reconciliation or authoritative clinical state. A displayed value is not made authoritative by its appearance in a dashboard.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Decoupled contextual interaction is a substantive Core responsibility that preserves the established information-access and control boundaries.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns support contextual discussion and human interaction with governed information and activity. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

Progress governed operational work in identifiable activity and temporal contexts.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}

Keep work progression and its timing intelligible across human and synthetic undertakings.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Work Order is human doing, To Do is human review/\allowbreak{}update/\allowbreak{}approval and Task is synthetic work. Projection does not own authoritative bookings or rosters.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Workflow \& Activity Coordination provides governed progression for three distinct work meanings: human operational Work Orders, human review or decision To Dos, and non-human Synthetic Tasks. It supports dispatch, state and deadline oversight without collapsing those meanings into a generic technical task. The common coordination responsibility makes progression visible while preserving who has authority to perform or decide the underlying activity.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Intent}

Keep assigned activity, acknowledgement, progress and outcome distinguishable across human and automated work.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Coordination does not confer clinical work ownership. Synthetic Tasks are not external clinical worklists, and the incomplete stalled/\allowbreak{}failed Process paths remain unresolved.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Governed activity progression is a substantive Core responsibility; information traceability preserves archetype, work and undertaking distinctions without transferring outcome authority.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns progress governed operational work in identifiable activity and temporal contexts. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Process Overview}

Work Order progression describes a human undertaking physical or operational activity. Assignment, acknowledgement and outcome make the undertaking accountable without collapsing dispatch into completion. Its generic work meaning can support different operational contexts while leaving their domain authority and the clinical-work boundary intact.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Workflow \& Activity Coordination}}



\item
\textbf{Activity Archetype}: \textbf{Human Doing} — physical or operational task executed by healthcare staff.



\item
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Created → Ready → Dispatched → Accepted → In-Progress → Completed /\allowbreak{} Failed /\allowbreak{} Cancelled



\item
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Created}}: Work order instantiated with scope, target, and required skills.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Ready}}: Preconditions satisfied; available for assignment.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Dispatched}}: Sent to target individual or worker group queue.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Accepted}}: Worker claims task.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Progress}}: Execution underway.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Completed}}: Task finished with recorded completion telemetry.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Process Overview}

To Do progression coordinates a human review or decision item. Completion records progression of the item, while the significance and authority of the resulting judgement depend on the governed activity. A review being marked complete therefore does not independently establish clinical adequacy, signing authority or an assurance conclusion.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Workflow \& Activity Coordination}}



\item
\textbf{Activity Archetype}: \textbf{Human Reviewing /\allowbreak{} Updating /\allowbreak{} Deciding} — clinical review, document countersignature, or administrative authorization task.



\item
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}:



\end{itemize}

\textit{RAD diagram: textual source notation.}
\begin{Verbatim}[breaklines,fontsize=\footnotesize]
graph LR
    I["Issued"] --> B["In-Inbox"]
    B --> R["Opened / Under-Review"]
    R --> A["Actioned / Decided"]
    D["Dismissed / Delegated<br/>Disposition/position unresolved"]
    NOTE["Illustrative progression, not a normative transition model.<br/>Relationship of dismissal/delegation to action/decision is unestablished."]
    classDef note fill:#fff8dc,stroke:#8a6d3b,stroke-dasharray:5 5;
    class NOTE,D note;
\end{Verbatim}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Issued}}: To Do generated (e.g., review abnormal potassium result).



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Inbox}}: Displayed in practitioner's actionable task list.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Opened / Under-Review}}: Clinician inspecting relevant clinical context.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Actioned / Decided}}: Decision executed (e.g., signed off, order placed, acknowledged).



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Dismissed / Delegated}}: Task reassigned to registrar or dismissed with comment.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Preserved uncertainty}: Whether dismissal/\allowbreak{}delegation is an alternative disposition, a subsequent action or a scoped variant remains unresolved; its disconnected diagram node establishes no transition or position in the illustrative progression.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Process Overview}

Synthetic Task progression concerns automated non-human execution, including waiting for a dependency and producing an output. It must remain distinct from human work orders and external clinical task lists. The disconnected stalled/\allowbreak{}failed outcome in the illustration leaves its relation to the success path unresolved; no reopening or post-completion failure transition is inferred.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Workflow \& Activity Coordination}}



\item
\textbf{Activity Archetype}: \textbf{Non-Human Executable Work} — automated system workflows, batch syndications, or policy evaluation tasks.



\item
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}:



\end{itemize}

\textit{RAD diagram: textual source notation.}
\begin{Verbatim}[breaklines,fontsize=\footnotesize]
graph LR
    D["Draft / Scheduled"] --> E["Executing"]
    E --> W["Awaiting-Dependency"]
    W --> C["Completed"]
    F["Progression Stalled / Failed<br/>Outcome/position unresolved"]
    NOTE["Illustrative progression, not a normative transition model.<br/>No Completed-to-Stalled/Failed transition is established."]
    classDef note fill:#fff8dc,stroke:#8a6d3b,stroke-dasharray:5 5;
    class NOTE,F note;
\end{Verbatim}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Draft / Scheduled}}: Automated task instantiated and scheduled for processing.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Executing}}: System actively processing task.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Awaiting-Dependency}}: Paused awaiting asynchronous external reply or event.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Completed}}: Automated execution succeeded and output artifact produced.



\item
\texttt{\seqsplit{Progression Stalled / Failed}}: Transient fault triggers scheduled recovery attempt; permanent failure records failure evidence.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Preserved uncertainty}: Whether stalled/\allowbreak{}failed is an alternative outcome, reopening/\allowbreak{}post-completion behaviour or a presentation defect remains unresolved. Its disconnected diagram node does not make success and failure equivalent or establish post-completion transitions.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Feature Overview}

A timeout or absent response leaves a materially significant outcome unknown. Reconciliation can confirm an effect, establish absence or retain uncertainty without automatically retrying the original work.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition — Proposed}

Reconcile indeterminate activity effects through authoritative observation before establishing a safe next disposition.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Boundary}

Execution uncertainty differs from insufficient assurance evidence; a retry does not prove the earlier attempt had no effect.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

This behaviour changes or exposes the bounded concern of Workflow \& Activity Coordination, rather than inheriting an adjacent responsibility.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Boundary}

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Calendar Management projects schedules and correlates events with temporal commitments. It brings rosters, on-call windows, facility calendars and appointment milestones into operational views without replacing their authoritative sources. This distinguishes the temporal context used for coordination from the business decisions that establish the schedule.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Projection does not author the roster or confer qualification, privilege or clinical assignment authority.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Consistent temporal projections and event correlation are direct platform coordination responsibilities.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns progress governed operational work in identifiable activity and temporal contexts. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Activity concerning the same patient, practitioner or bed needs a coherent entity-relative frame. Interest fan-out, serial progression, fresh information context and uncertain effects remain distinguishable from generic multi-work-unit progression.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition — Proposed}

Coordinate governed operational progression relative to one represented entity, including interested behaviour participation and controlled recovery.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Intent}

Keep the progression of one represented entity coherent across interested operational behaviours.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Entity coordination does not own all entity information, determine clinical work or become the source of clinical decisions. No Twin component allocation follows from this proposal.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Review Confidence}
Medium; applies to the proposal, not to preserved canonical meaning.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Derivation Provenance}
Inferred from bounded responsibilities and their semantic decomposition. AI architectural synthesis under the explicitly authorised Step 2 task \hyperref[evidence:ec6250f7cf7c29a5]{DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md:73}; \hyperref[evidence:27549d51551beae6]{architectural-axioms.md:742}

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Feature Overview}

Failure may stop a behaviour, an input or the entity progression and may leave effects uncertain. Resumption must preserve that distinction rather than imply rollback or automatic safe retry.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition — Proposed}

Apply explicit behaviour-failure dispositions and controlled, authorised resumption for entity-relative processing.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Boundary}

Recovery cannot silently declare no effects, bypass governance or resume a halted entity automatically.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

This behaviour changes or exposes the bounded concern of Entity-Specific Operational Coordination, rather than inheriting an adjacent responsibility.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

An activity needs a fulfilment definition even when only one bounded execution unit is involved. This capability specifies its semantic envelope while execution and event delivery remain separate responsibilities.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition — Proposed}

Define the information context, expected outcomes, continuation conditions and housekeeping of governed operational activity.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Intent}

Make the expected information and fulfilment basis of an undertaking explicit before it executes.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

An activity definition is neither an orchestrator nor a choreographer. It does not choose clinical care or dynamically invent execution logic.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Review Confidence}
Medium; applies to the proposal, not to preserved canonical meaning.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Derivation Provenance}
Inferred from bounded responsibilities and their semantic decomposition. AI architectural synthesis under the explicitly authorised Step 2 task \hyperref[evidence:ea0c62dfd5edfd4a]{context-and-persistence-management.md:52}; \hyperref[evidence:cb9909df0650a902]{pathways-journeys-and-handoff.md:37}

\cataloguefield{section}{Capability Overview}

The frame separates design and criteria stewardship from the evaluation activity that produces findings. It preserves the established three assurance capabilities and five Functions without turning observation or operational health into an assurance conclusion.


\cataloguefield{section}{Definition — Proposed}

Specify how governed service behaviour is assured and independently establish what applicable evidence demonstrates.


\cataloguefield{section}{Intent}

Establish justified confidence in governed service behaviour without giving the subject control of its own assurance conclusion.


\cataloguefield{section}{Boundary}

Assurance cannot manage, remediate or approve its subject merely because it observes it. Clinical adequacy, financial governance and source-information authority remain outside this mandate.


\cataloguefield{section}{Derivation Provenance}
Inferred from bounded responsibilities and their semantic decomposition. AI architectural synthesis under the explicitly authorised Step 2 task \hyperref[evidence:4bac85accd34ce0b]{business-architecture-metamodel.md:49}; \hyperref[evidence:be61392fefb4bb10]{information-responsibility.md:10}; \hyperref[evidence:14c8f26d232fcb78]{health-service-assurance.md:9}

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Assurance Design determines how satisfaction of a governed requirement or expected behaviour will be assured. It makes the disposition, criteria, evidence and evaluation expectations explicit alongside behaviour and failure/\allowbreak{}recovery design. Its output is a basis for assurance rather than proof that the implemented behaviour has satisfied the requirement.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

The capability to determine and define how satisfaction of a governed requirement, constraint or expected behaviour will be assured, including its assurance disposition, applicable criteria, required evidence and evaluation expectations.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Designing assurance does not confer approval authority, define the underlying obligation or allocate a runtime component. No Feature decomposition or CT ancestry is established.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance — v0.1 explanation}

Formal classification remains Unresolved. Its approved support to Health Service Assurance establishes purpose and Enterprise Capability contributions without adjudicating this separate relevance dimension.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns model how satisfaction will be assured and maintain applicable, temporally qualified criteria. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Function Overview}

Designing service assurance turns a requirement's assurance question into an explicit disposition and evaluation basis. The modeller determines how satisfaction is to be assessed, not what the authoritative requirement should mean or who may approve it. Design completion is not evidence that the implemented behaviour satisfies that requirement.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Design Service Assurance}}.



\item
\textbf{Definition}: Defines how satisfaction of a governed requirement, constraint or expected behaviour is to be independently established, including the applicable assurance disposition, assurance criteria, required evidence and evaluation expectations.



\item
\textbf{Boundary}: Concerns assurance design. It does not establish the underlying governance requirement, grant authority to it, perform the resulting assurance, manage the subject activity or prescribe application or implementation mechanisms. Modelling the resulting Assurance Definition does not grant approval authority. The Strategy peer relationship to behaviour design and failure/\allowbreak{}recovery design creates no additional Capability or Function.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Preserved v0.1 Review Matters}

No contextual-view placement is established.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Process Overview}

Assurance design establishes a reusable basis for how satisfaction will be evaluated, rather than running the evaluation itself. Criteria-management participation retains its separate owner and does not create an exchange Service or a shared criteria lifecycle. An Assurance Definition can be reused, so each execution need not imply a freshly performed Design Process.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Assurance Process Design}}.



\item
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md\#assurance-design}{Assurance Design}.



\item
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Establishes and maintains how satisfaction of a governed requirement, constraint or expected behaviour is to be assured.



\item
\textbf{Principal Performing Role}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/actors-roles/roles.md\#service-assurance-modeller}{Service Assurance Modeller}.



\item
\textbf{Participating Functions}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#design-service-assurance}{Design Service Assurance} and \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#manage-assurance-criteria}{Manage Assurance Criteria}. Manage Assurance Criteria retains ownership within Assurance Criteria Management; its participation does not subsume that Capability's criteria lifecycle or transfer its information responsibility to Assurance Design.



\item
\textbf{Conceptual Output}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#42-assurance-definition--conceptual-modelling-output}{Assurance Definition}, retaining its conceptual Business Architecture output/\allowbreak{}boundary treatment.



\item
\textbf{Boundary}: Governance Authority establishes what is authoritative. Design does not grant Service Assurance Modeller approval authority. Detailed Assurance Definition lifecycle, approval/\allowbreak{}publication workflows, criteria lifecycle and information modelling remain unresolved. Participation of the two Functions does not establish a cross-capability lifecycle or a new exchange/\allowbreak{}Service between their owners.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Assurance Criteria Management maintains reusable evaluative criteria with governed standing and temporal applicability. Version and effective context matter because a conclusion must be understood against the criteria applicable to the subject and time being assessed. Criteria may operationalise governing requirements, but their management is not authority to change those requirements.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

The capability to establish and manage reusable, governed and temporally identifiable assurance criteria through which subjects may be evaluated.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Modelling criteria does not inherently approve them. Detailed criterion states and approval workflows remain unresolved, and criteria need not all originate in formal Governance.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance — v0.1 explanation}

Formal relevance remains Unresolved. Established assurance support explains the enabling purpose without classifying it by inference or allocating software responsibility.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns model how satisfaction will be assured and maintain applicable, temporally qualified criteria. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Function Overview}

Criteria management maintains the reusable evaluative basis and its temporal standing. It permits an assessment to be understood against the criterion applicable at the relevant time, rather than today's unqualified version. Management of that basis does not inherently grant approval authority or permit alteration of the governing obligation.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Manage Assurance Criteria}}.



\item
\textbf{Definition}: Establishes and manages reusable, governed and temporally identifiable assurance criteria through which governed subjects may be evaluated.



\item
\textbf{Scope}: Criteria may express governance rule boundaries, quality constraints, performance expectations, compliance criteria, temporal criteria, evidence requirements or completeness expectations. These examples are not an exhaustive taxonomy. Criteria may have lifecycle, version and temporal applicability.



\item
\textbf{Boundary}: Managing a criterion does not transfer authority for the governing requirement from which it may derive. Criteria may operationalise a requirement without silently altering, weakening, strengthening or replacing it; not every criterion must derive from formal Governance. Modelling/\allowbreak{}managing criteria does not inherently confer approval authority. Detailed criterion lifecycle states and approval workflows remain unresolved.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Preserved v0.1 Review Matters}

No contextual-view placement is established.

\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}

Governed Assurance independently evaluates a subject through applicable criteria and trustworthy evidence, establishing explicit findings and conclusions. Context establishment associates source-owned information with a particular assurance purpose; assessment evaluates it; adjudication establishes the supported outcome. Insufficient evidence remains a meaningful limit rather than a forced positive or negative result.


The capability can manage its own assurance activity without managing the subject. Request, progression status and established outcome are different client concerns; the requester does not thereby control the evaluation or gain unrestricted status access.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

The capability to independently evaluate a governed subject against applicable assurance criteria through the assembly and evaluation of sufficient trustworthy evidence, establishing explicit findings, exceptions and assurance conclusions.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

No remediation, assignment or operational escalation of the subject is acquired. Financial governance is deliberately excluded; assurance does not recursively assure its own execution, and no component allocation is established.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance — v0.1 explanation}

Formal classification remains Unresolved. The approved independent-assurance responsibility and contribution model establish material purpose without resolving that metadata dimension.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The responsibility concerns associate trustworthy evidence, assess it and adjudicate independently reportable findings about governed service behaviour. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Function Overview}

Context establishment makes particular source-owned information evidence for a particular assurance purpose, with applicable subject, criteria and time identified. It includes evidence assembly without assuming sufficiency or prescribing copying and storage. This contextual evidentiary association is the assurance responsibility; ownership of the source material remains unchanged.


\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Establish Assurance Context}}.



\item
\textbf{Definition}: Establishes the governed subject, applicable assurance purpose and criteria, relevant temporal context, and contextual association of sufficient trustworthy source information as evidence required for an assurance activity.



\item
\textbf{Scope}: Includes the evidence-assembly responsibility previously described as Assurance Evidence Assembly; no separate evidence-assembly Function is established. Sufficiency is required for conclusion, not assumed merely because context is established; unavailable or insufficient evidence remains explicit.



\item
\textbf{Information Boundary}: Source information remains owned by its responsible source Capability. Its use as evidence does not transfer ownership or originating authority. Governed Assurance owns the contextual association that particular information constitutes evidence for a particular assurance purpose. Evidence association and applicable criteria may each be temporal and version-specific; association distinguishes the information state relevant to assurance from its current state.



\item
\textbf{Realisation Boundary}: Uses generic EC-02 context-management capability together with EC-14 assurance-specific semantics as documented in \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#41-context-management-contribution}{§4.1}. Establishment of Assurance Context prescribes no copying, persistence, aggregation, caching or other technical mechanism.



\end{itemize}




\cataloguefield{paragraph}{Preserved v0.1 Review Matters}

No contextual-view placement is established.
